messages:
sanjay: FYI I'm seeing a surge of 502/504s from IPv6 clients to /api/ingest over the last 20m :eyes:
eli: confirmed on our dashboards, spikes line up with a Route53 change earlier today?
maya: which change? I didn't touch any DNS today. Link to SLO graphs?
sanjay: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ingress/edge-errors?from=-20m to=now — look at client_ip_family=6 series
marie: I pulled a few logs, e.g. from one request: `upstream response timeout or connection reset by peer` and curl -6 shows `HTTP/2 502` but curl -4 returns 200.
sanjay: reproducer: `curl -6 -vvvv https://ingest.redwood.ai/v1/test` -> connection established to LB IPv6, then `recv()` from backend failed.
eli: sounds like LB -> node path for IPv6 isn't matching node egress config. Are nodes dual-stack? I think our nodepools are IPv4-only and we rely on NAT64 for IPv6 -> IPv4 translation in some regions.
maya: NAT64 gateway in eu-west-1 had high CPU earlier, ops alerted. Could be dropping translations under load. That would explain IPv6-only clients failing while IPv4 clients OK.
marie: healthchecks are weird too: the LB sometimes reports backend as healthy via IPv4 but fails over IPv6 path intermittently. Might be a mismatch between our load balancer dualstack mode and the node service ipFamilies.
sanjay: quick mitigation idea: remove AAAA record for ingest.prod.redwood.ai until we stabilize, fallback to IPv4-only. That'll drop native IPv6 clients to IPv4 via carrier NAT but reduce 502s. Thoughts?
eli: agree as a quick mitigation. But we should also fix the root cause — either ensure nodes actually support dual-stack or force LB to prefer IPv4 for backend connections.
maya: can we add an annotation to the k8s Service to force the AWS NLB to not advertise AAAA? external-dns created both A+AAAA from the LB's dualstack config.
marie: snippet to temporarily override external-dns: `external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname: ingest.prod.redwood.ai.` and set `external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/ipv6: "false"` (we have a short-lived internal fork that supports that flag)
eli: action list: 1) @maria (maya) remove AAAA from Route53 for prod ingest. 2) @eli check NAT64 gateway/translation metrics and scale if saturated. 3) @marie add ingress/service annotation so external-dns doesn't recreate AAAA. 4) infra ticket to evaluate long-term: either full dual-stack nodes or keep IPv4-only + NAT64 with proper autoscaling.
marie: I'll patch external-dns and open a PR, can do canary to staging first.
maya: I'm going to manually delete the AAAA record in Route53 now, will coordinate with DNS propagation check.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered by marie/external-dns-flag -> CI passed -> rollout started :rocket:
infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-4328 "ingest: intermittent IPv6 -> backend connection failures; evaluate dual-stack mismatch" and assigned to @eli and @maria
eli: updated NAT64 ASG to +2 instances in eu-west-1, watching metrics. If that fixes it we should still plan for a less brittle architecture.
sanjay: after Route53 AAAA deletion errors dropped to baseline within ~3m. Good short-term. Need postmortem and clear decision path on whether we enable real dual-stack nodepools.
marie: Agreed. I'll own the postmortem and propose 3 options (dual-stack nodes, managed NAT64 with autoscale and redundancy, or IPv4-only with documented DNS policy).
maya: tagging oncall for visibility @oncall-maya FYI :wave:
eli: also check healthcheck config — ensure LB healthchecks are sent on IPv4 path or we use cross-protocol consistency so LB doesn't mark endpoints healthy only on one family.
sanjay: TL;DR: removed AAAA as quick fix, scaled NAT64 as mitigation, created INFRA-4328, next steps PR for external-dns and a postmortem + architecture decision. :thumbsup:
